Printed at the bottom of the dial is KISHI KAISEI (起死回生), an old Japanese expression that literally means “to rise from death and return to life.” It is used to describe a dramatic turnaround—overcoming great hardship and finding success after facing what once seemed like a hopeless situation. That idea is reflected throughout the Shell 98. Its distressed case, aged dial, and worn appearance symbolize a life shaped by challenges rather than perfection. Every scratch, mark, and sign of wear represents obstacles overcome, making the watch a tribute to resilience, perseverance, and the strength to move forward despite adversity. The Shell 98 measures 36mm. Although its case shape is Explorer-inspired, it has always reminded me of a turtle shell, hence the name “Shell.” The “98” comes from the number I originally used to represent 1998 in the first reel in which the watch appeared. Each vintage-inspired Shiro Kara timepiece is handcrafted individually, one at a time, and the watch shown is the exact piece its owner will receive. While the same design may be commissioned again, no two watches will ever develop the same character. Due to the nature of my hand-aging techniques, every patina develops uniquely throughout the process, giving each watch its own personality and story. Every vintage Shiro Kara is truly one of one. — Shiro Kara 🍮

watches.name: Shiro Kara Vintage (SKV) Diver: Sabumarina Taro
watches.description: SOLD: ARMAN P 🇺🇸 3/2/26 Unit no: 1st Unit no. 1 Available: 1 The Sabumarina サブマリーナ Taro is a no-date, vintage Submariner style dive watch that brings together all the classic design elements. It features Mercedes hands, a domed acrylic crystal, and an Oyster-style bracelet. The dial, hands, and bezel insert are carefully aged, giving the watch a true vintage feel as if it has passed through decades of use. This concept inspired the creation of this model, where different parts come together to create diverse and imaginative variations while still sharing that signature white silver vintage dial. For this timepiece, I began by aging the silver-white dial, giving it a subtle patina that adds depth and character while setting the stage for the watch’s vintage aesthetic. Paired with a green bezel insert I carefully aged it to create a naturally worn look. The goal was to achieve an organic, authentic pattern—something that feels like it has developed over time rather than being artificially distressed. To complement this, I matched the lume pip to the aged hour markers, ensuring everything worked together to enhance the vintage feel. The finishing touch for the dial was the classic Mercedes handset, which I also aged to blend seamlessly with the overall aesthetic. The bracelet is a timeless Jubilee style, deliberately scratched to give it the charm of a pre-loved, well-traveled piece.
